\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{крыса} (krýsa)}{крыса (krýsa)}]{\ru{крыса} (krýsa) — a rat}

\label{lesson:RU-C196-krysa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a rose, then the Russian for an oak.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{крыса}}
\textbf{\ru{крыса}} (\emph{krýsa}) — \textquotedblleft{}a rat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{крыса}} — Vasmer finds none of the existing explanations reliable: a reshaping of the root of \emph{\ru{грызть}}, \textquotedblleft{}to gnaw\textquotedblright{}, links with \emph{\ru{крот}}, \textquotedblleft{}mole\textquotedblright{}, or \emph{\ru{кровь}}, \textquotedblleft{}blood\textquotedblright{}, and others.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{паук} (paúk)}{паук (paúk)}]{\ru{паук} (paúk) — a spider}

\label{lesson:RU-C196-pauk}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for an oak, then the Russian for a rat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{паук}}
\textbf{\ru{паук}} (\emph{paúk}) — \textquotedblleft{}a spider\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{паук}} is \emph{\ru{па}-} with \emph{*ǫkŭ}, \textquotedblleft{}a hook\textquotedblright{}, for the spider's bent legs (Vasmer). Vasmer relates the root to Greek \emph{ónkos}, \textquotedblleft{}a hook\textquotedblright{}, and Latin \emph{uncus}, \textquotedblleft{}hooked\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{комар} (komár)}{комар (komár)}]{\ru{комар} (komár) — a mosquito}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a rat, then the Russian for a spider.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{комар}}
\textbf{\ru{комар}} (\emph{komár}) — \textquotedblleft{}a mosquito\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{комар}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*komarŭ} — inherited. Vasmer relates it to Lithuanian \emph{kamãnė}, \textquotedblleft{}a bumblebee\textquotedblright{}, and Old Prussian \emph{camus}, \textquotedblleft{}bumblebee\textquotedblright{}, and probably Middle High German \emph{hummen}, \textquotedblleft{}to hum\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{муха} (múkha)}{муха (múkha)}]{\ru{муха} (múkha) — a fly}

\label{lesson:RU-C196-mukha}

Before the new one: say the Russian for a spider, then the Russian for a mosquito.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{муха}}
\textbf{\ru{муха}} (\emph{múkha}) — \textquotedblleft{}a fly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{муха}} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Slavic \emph{*muxa} — inherited, with \emph{\ru{мошка}}, \textquotedblleft{}a midge\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer). Latin \emph{musca}, \textquotedblleft{}fly\textquotedblright{}, and Greek \emph{muîa}, \textquotedblleft{}fly\textquotedblright{}, go back to the same PIE word.
\end{cousinweb}
